 def decide(observation, tools):
+    # Get the two old camera poses and their headings
+    views = observation['views']
+    if len(views) < 2:
+        return 0, 'right', {}
+
+    # Extract the two old frames
+    view0 = views[0]
+    view1 = views[1]
+
+    # Extract heading, pitch, and relative positions
+    h0 = view0['heading']
+    h1 = view1['heading']
+    pitch0 = view0['pitch']
+    pitch1 = view1['pitch']
+    right0 = view0['right_of_end_m']
+    forward0 = view0['forward_of_end_m']
+    right1 = view1['right_of_end_m']
+    forward1 = view1['forward_of_end_m']
+
+    # Get movement history
+    movement = observation['movement']
+    # We assume the robot walks forward and may turn once to reveal the target
+
+    # Use direct turn logits to decide which way to turn
     scores = tools.direct()
-    return 0, 'right' if scores[1] > scores[0] else 'left', {}
+    if scores[1] > scores[0]:
+        return 1, 'right', {}
+    elif scores[0] > scores[1]:
+        return 1, 'left', {}
+    else:
+        # If no clear preference, use visual evidence from locate and point
+        # Try to estimate the target's forward direction using locate and point
+        ranges = tools.locate()
+        if ranges[0] > 0 or ranges[1] > 0:
+            # Use the point data to estimate object position
+            points = tools.point()
+            if points[0] is not None and points[1] is not None:
+                # Both frames have point data
+                p0 = points[0]
+                p1 = points[1]
+                # If the point is in the same relative position, the direction may be consistent
+                # Check if the horizontal position changed
+                if p0[0] > 0.5 and p1[0] > 0.5:
+                    return 1, 'right', {}
+                elif p0[0] < 0.5 and p1[0] < 0.5:
+                    return 1, 'left', {}
+                else:
+                    # Unclear, use direct scores again
+                    return 1, 'right' if scores[1] > scores[0] else 'left', {}
+            else:
+                # Only one point available, use the one with higher confidence
+                if points[0] is not None:
+                    return 1, 'right' if points[0][0] > 0.5 else 'left', {}
+                elif points[1] is not None:
+                    return 1, 'right' if points[1][0] > 0.5 else 'left', {}
+        else:
+            # No locate detection, fall back to direct
+            return 1, 'right' if scores[1] > scores[0] else 'left', {}
